content: Lost-update race condition: the version check (read) and the write are separate, non-atomic steps and there is no `@Transactional`/conditional UPDATE. Two devices saving concurrently both read version=1, both pass the `serverV != clientV` check, and both write — the second write silently overwrites the first (version becomes 2 instead of 3), so the "optimistic lock" contract is not actually enforced. Use an atomic conditional update and verify the affected row count (e.g. `UPDATE biz_form_draft SET draft_data=?, version=version+1 WHERE id=? AND version=?`, retry/throw 409 when 0 rows), or enable MyBatis-Plus `@Version` optimistic locking with `OptimisticLockerInnerInterceptor`.

Wrap the save in a transaction and handle the duplicate-key case by re-reading and retrying/raising a 409 conflict.

content: `URLDecoder.decode` implements application/x-www-form-urlencoded semantics, in which `+` is decoded to a space. In a URI *path* a `+` is a literal character, so any oss_key/filename containing `+` (or `%2B`) will be mis-resolved and the lookup/`UrlResource` will silently 404. The same pattern is duplicated in `downloadPublic` below. Prefer an encoding-aware, non-form decoder (e.g. `org.springframework.web.util.UriUtils.decode(..., StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`).

The broad `catch (Exception e)` discards the exception without any logging, so genuine server-side failures (malformed URI, I/O error, DB error from `getFileByKey`/`canDownloadFile`) are silently reported to the client as 404 and become impossible to diagnose. Log the exception (`log.warn`/`log.error`) and/or narrow the catch to the expected encoding exceptions.

content:
The `#{tenantId} IS NULL OR tenant_id = #{tenantId}` fallback defeats the stated goal of this change ("显式租户条件…跨租户清库收口"). In MySQL `NULL IS NULL` evaluates to TRUE, so when `tenantId` is null the OR-branch short-circuits and the statement becomes `DELETE FROM biz_score_participant WHERE period = ?` — i.e. it physically wipes ALL tenants' participant lists for that period. Callers can and do pass null: `ScoreService` line 232 passes `GroupScopeUtil.currentGroupOrNull()`, which returns null both for the platform admin and for a non-admin whose group cannot be resolved (see `GroupScopeUtil` javadoc: "取不到任何集团归属 → null, 调用方必须按 fail-closed 处理(空结果/拒绝)"). Because the mapper cannot distinguish those two cases, a fail-closed situation is silently converted into the most destructive possible cross-tenant delete, and this also bypasses the MyBatis-Plus tenant interceptor (which is deliberately disabled when `aigicrm.tenant.enable=false`, as the entry-mapper comment notes). Recommend making the null case fail-closed (delete nothing) and letting callers that legitimately need a cross-tenant/admin cleanup use a separate, explicitly named method, e.g.:

```java
@Delete("<script>DELETE FROM biz_score_participant WHERE period = #{period}"
        + "<if test='tenantId != null'> AND tenant_id = #{tenantId}</if>"
        + "<if test='tenantId == null'> AND 1 = 0</if></script>")
int physicalDeleteByPeriod(@Param("period") String period, @Param("tenantId") Long tenantId);
```

content: Mass-assignment risk: the request body is bound directly to the persistence entity and then merged by id, so a caller with `system:config:edit` can overwrite fields that should be server-controlled — notably `builtIn`. Because `SysDictService.deleteType` only blocks deletion when `builtIn == 1`, a client can first PUT `{"builtIn":0}` to this endpoint (or POST it in `createType`/`createData`) and then DELETE the type, bypassing the "系统内置字典不允许删除" protection. `dictCode`/`status`/`createdAt` can likewise be tampered with. Suggest whitelisting the updatable fields (dedicated DTO / explicit setters) and forcing `builtIn`/`createdAt` on the server side.

The value resolved from `DICT_COLUMN_MAP` is only compared against the literal "industry"; every other mapping falls into the `else` branch and writes `dev_type`. So the map is effectively a hardcoded 2-branch switch, and if anyone adds a third mapping (e.g. "customer_type" -> "customer_type"), `updateData` will silently overwrite the wrong customer column (`dev_type`) instead of the intended one. The ternary is also duplicated for `.eq` and `.set`. Consider mapping the dict code directly to the target `SFunction`/column and using it once, e.g.:

```java
private static final Map<String, SFunction<BizCustomer, ?>> DICT_COLUMN_MAP = Map.of(
        "industry", BizCustomer::getIndustry,
        "dev_type", BizCustomer::getDevType);
```

and then apply it via `.eq(column, oldValue).set(column, newValue)`.

content: N+1 queries: one JDBC round-trip per position and per role code, executed on the login path (`UserDetailsServiceImpl` calls this). For a user with many positions/roles this becomes dozens of queries. Prefer a single batched query, e.g. `... WHERE assignee_type='POSITION' AND assignee_key IN (?,?,...)` (build the placeholders from the list) and one for ROLE.

Loop body always exits on the first iteration (cache hit → `return`, DB branch → `return`, DB failure → `throw`), so any roleCode after the first is unreachable. Consequence: if the user's first role has no `role_perm_scope` row, the scope is silently defaulted to OWNER and a later role that legitimately configures ORG is ignored — while `lookup`/`configuredScopes` iterate ALL roles. This makes the anchor inconsistent with the scope resolution and can silently narrow/widen the resolved range. Suggest iterating all roles and only falling back to OWNER after none of them has a row (i.e. `if (rows.isEmpty()) continue;`).

`anchor` is part of the table's unique key `uk_assignee_ma (assignee_type, assignee_key, module, action, anchor)` (V1 baseline / V9), so this UPSERT does NOT update on an anchor change — switching a config from OWNER to ORG inserts a second row instead, leaving a stale row for the same (assignee, module, action). `lookup` (`SELECT scope_level ... LIMIT 1`) and `anchorOf` (`SELECT anchor ... LIMIT 1`) use no ORDER BY, so which row wins becomes non-deterministic and the effective scope/anchor can flip after any DB re-read. Suggest deleting/upserting all rows for the same (assignee_type, assignee_key, module, action) before insert, or reading with a deterministic `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`.

content: `size` comes straight from the HTTP request param (`@RequestParam(defaultValue = "20") int size`) and only an upper bound is applied. When `size` is negative (e.g. `?size=-1`), MyBatis-Plus's `PaginationInnerInterceptor` treats a negative size as "no pagination" and skips the LIMIT clause, so an authenticated user can pull the whole append-only `sys_rule_version` table in one request (and a size of 0 returns an empty/undefined page). Clamp the lower bound as well, e.g. `Math.max(1, Math.min(size, MAX_PAGE_SIZE))`.

content: Check-then-act race: two concurrent `create` calls with the same `code` can both see `count == 0` and pass the validation. The DB has `UNIQUE KEY uk_code` on `sys_permission_rule.code`, so the second insert will throw `DuplicateKeyException` (HTTP 500) rather than the intended `BusinessException("规则编码已存在")`. Suggest relying on the unique constraint and translating the violation, e.g. wrap `ruleMapper.insert(rule)` in a try/catch for `org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException` and rethrow as `BusinessException` (the pre-check can stay as a fast path).

`update` is missing the two guards that `create` performs:
1) No existence check — if `id` does not exist (or is null, e.g. a malformed body), `updateById` silently affects 0 rows and the method still returns success while pointlessly wiping the permission cache and bumping every user's `perm_version`.
2) No uniqueness check on `code` — the controller sets id from the path but lets the body carry any `code`, so renaming a rule to an already used code will hit the DB `uk_code` unique index and surface as an unhandled `DuplicateKeyException` (HTTP 500) instead of the friendly `BusinessException("规则编码已存在")` used in `create`.
Also, since the whole entity comes straight from `@RequestBody`, null required fields (name/code/targetEntity/ruleType) are not validated and will fail at the DB NOT NULL constraint.
`getById` is never referenced anywhere: `SysPermissionRuleController` only exposes list/create/update/delete. It is effectively dead code — either wire it to a detail endpoint or remove it.

content: This runs on every rule create/update/delete and updates the entire `sys_user` table (no WHERE clause), so with a large user table each low-frequency admin action becomes a full-table write (row locks, binlog volume, replication lag). It also deliberately invalidates the permission cache of every user, forcing a full permission-context rebuild on their next request. Note the migrations use `WHERE deleted = 0` for the same statement, so the filter is at least inconsistent here. Suggest adding `WHERE deleted = 0` and, because the identical method is duplicated in `SysDeptService`, `SysRoleService` and `RolePermScopeService`, extracting it into a single shared component that encapsulates the cache eviction + version bump.
suggestion_code: jdbc.update("UPDATE sys_user SET perm_version = perm_version + 1 WHERE deleted = 0");
existing_code: jdbc.update("UPDATE sys_user SET perm_version = perm_version + 1");

content: Unlike every other entity in this project (e.g. `BizCustomer`, `BizContact`, `SysUser`, which annotate the audit columns with `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT)` / `@TableField(fill = FieldFill.INSERT_UPDATE)`), `BizTask` declares `createdAt`/`updatedAt` without fill annotations. The registered `MetaObjectHandler.metaObjectHandler()` uses `strictInsertFill`/`strictUpdateFill`, which only populate fields that carry a fill strategy, so these fields stay null on the entity instance after insert/update. `TaskController` returns `taskViewService.toRow(taskService.createFromMap(body))` and `TaskViewService.toRow` exposes `createdAt`, so the create response always returns `createdAt: null` even though the DB has a default. Add the fill annotations to keep behavior consistent with the rest of the codebase (the DB default then no longer silently hides the gap).

content: `countByModule` issues 6 separate `selectCount` statements (1 for "全部" + 5 in this loop). Worse, every `buildBase()` call re-runs `scopeResolver.resolveModuleUsersWithinGroup(...)`, which itself performs permission evaluation and a `GroupScopeUtil.userIdsInGroup(jdbcTemplate, ...)` SQL query — so a single HTTP request to `/api/system/logs/counts` may trigger up to ~12 DB round trips for identical permission data, and the "全部" count is just the sum the DB should compute. Suggest resolving the visible-scope wrapper once and issuing a single `GROUP BY module` aggregate (e.g. `selectMaps` with `.select(SysLog::getModule)` + `groupBy`), then deriving both the per-module map and the total in memory.

`size` comes straight from the request (`@RequestParam(defaultValue = "15")`) and is not clamped here, and no `maxLimit` is configured on `PaginationInnerInterceptor` (MybatisPlusConfig). A caller can therefore pass an arbitrarily large `size` (e.g. `size=1000000`) and force loading/returning the whole `sys_log` table in one request. Clamp the page parameters in the service (e.g. `size = Math.min(Math.max(size, 1), 200)`).

content: This branch is a fail-open no-op: if a non-admin ever reaches it, no `userId` predicate is added and the query returns the operation logs of the entire platform (exactly the ACL-P1-001 class of bug this code was meant to fix). The comment asserts the invariant is guaranteed by `resolveModuleUsersWithinGroup` (currently true, since that method only returns `null` for users holding the admin role), but the correctness of this security filter then depends silently on a remote method's contract — one refactor of the resolver and audit logs leak platform-wide. Make it fail-closed by default, e.g. treat `null` the same as an empty set (`w.eq(SysLog::getUserId, Long.MIN_VALUE)`) or throw an `IllegalStateException`.

`LocalDate.parse` throws `DateTimeParseException` for any non-`yyyy-MM-dd` value, which is not caught anywhere in this layer and will surface as a 500 error for a simple bad query parameter. There is also no check that `startDate <= endDate` (a reversed range silently returns an empty page). Consider validating the parameters first (parse once, return an empty result or a `Result.error` for malformed/reversed ranges) instead of propagating the runtime exception.

循环内逐次调用 `deptMapper.selectDescendantIds(orgId)`，每次都是一条独立 SQL（N+1）。组织管理员管辖多个组织、且目标部门不在可见列表时，会放大成 N 条递归查询。建议先一次性收集 `getCurrentManagedOrgIds()`，再用一条带 `IN` 的递归/SQL 查询批量取回所有后代部门 ID，最后在内存中判断 `contains(targetDeptId)`。
